maria: Ran a 60s nsys trace on the 8k long-chat workload this morning. seeing a new hotspot that wasn't in last week's baseline. attaching quick summary below.

raj: ugh, which kernel is the culprit?

maria: Top 5 by GPU time (nsys aggregated):
- 36.2%: kv_prefetch_write_kernel_v3
- 16.8%: fused_attn_gemm_v2
- 11.5%: softmax_block_v1
- 9.2%: kv_cache_apply_mask
- 7.0%: rms_norm_shard

oliver: kv_prefetch_write_kernel_v3?? that's new naming — looks like the prefetch path we landed last week.

jen: is it possible prefetch turned into a synchronous store path under certain batch shapes?

maria: that's my suspicion. timeline shows kv_prefetch_write running on stream 4 and blocking stream 0 more than expected. perfetto slice shows long tail and lots of small launches (~200-400us each).

perf-bot: [perf regression detector] alert: +28% GPU time on kv_prefetch_write_kernel_v3 compared to baseline (1791800000).

liang: can you paste the nsys command you used? want to repro locally.

maria: sure:```bash
nsys profile --output=kv-prefetch-8k --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --cpuctxsw=1 --duration=60 --capture-range=nvtx
nsys stats kv-prefetch-8k.qdrep --report gputrace --format json > kv-trace.json
```
I then ran a small jq pipeline to get kernel times.

oliver: do you have metrics for occupancy/SM util for that kernel? that's the smoking gun for backpressure.

maria: yes — overall SM util for that kernel is high (~92%) but achieved occupancy is low (24%). registers/wave limits look suspicious.

jen: high SM util with low occupancy usually means long-running single-thread blocks or stalls (divergence/L2 wait). could be atomics or serialized stores.

raj: any differences in launch params? block size or grid from the new prefetch code?

maria: launch config didn't change: (block=128, grid = dynamic per batch). But we now do a small 64B write per key with an atomic<>update path when cache miss. atomicAdd is used in kv_prefetch_write_kernel_v3 for write aggregation.

liang: atomic patterns explain long tail. On Ampere/Blackwell, atomics to L2 can serialize if many warps collide. If batch shapes produce hot keys, you'll see the skew.

oliver: can we confirm key distribution skew in the trace? maybe local batching heuristic now groups similar keys.

maria: I pulled a quick distribution from the same run: top 1% of keys account for ~38% of prefetch writes. So yes, skewed.

jen: two orthogonal fixes: 1) change prefetch to use per-warp buffers + reduce atomics, 2) randomize write aggregation (hash+reduce) to spread L2 banks.

raj: before code changes, can we validate by turning off prefetch or routing those writes to a separate stream so they don't stall critical path?

maria: tried separate stream (stream 7) — that reduced blocking but increased overall GPU time by ~6% (more context switches and small kernels fragmented).

liang: fragmentation cost is expected. Another experiment: coarsen prefetch aggregation so we do fewer larger writes. fewer launches -> less kernel launch overhead and lower atomic contention.

maria: added a quick macro to coalesce 8 keys per threadblock and re-ran; result: kv_prefetch_write fraction dropped to 19%, tail reduced 3x, and end-to-end p99 latency improved 14%.

perf-bot: [note] experiment: coalesced-prefetch-8 reduced KV kernel launches from ~12k to ~1.4k in 60s sample.

oliver: nice. so root cause is a combination of (A) key skew and (B) fine-grained prefetch writes creating many atomics + kernel-launch overhead -> SM backpressure.

jen: next: we should instrument kernel to emit counters for per-warp atomic collisions (simple counter increment path) and add a guardrail in batching heuristic to avoid grouping highly similar keys into same micro-batch.

maria: creating a small patch to: 1) add coarse aggregation mode behind feature flag, 2) add NVTX markers for prefetch begin/end, and 3) emit a perfcounter to S3 for offline analysis. will open PR.

liang: also recommend kernel-level tweak: replace atomicAdd on 64-bit with warp-level reduce + one atomic per warp. reduces contention.

raj: timeline for rollout?

maria: I'll push a draft PR today, run perf off a subset of clusters tomorrow, and if stable, roll to canary next week.

oliver: one more ask — can you dump the top-20 kernels by total_time and avg_duration for the trace so we can publish a quick perf note? I can do the visualization.

maria: done, added CSV to the PR artifacts.

perf-bot: [action] open_ticket: PERF-923 kv_prefetch contention; assignee: maria; priority: P2.

jen: thanks all. this was a useful diff from the baseline. main takeaways documented in the PR description. :thumbsup:

maria: I'll follow up with perf graphs and the PR link in this thread when ready.
